blocks.text: After completing this module, you will be able to
1. Manage customer interactions in a professional way
2. Apply basic conflict resolution techniques with customers
3. Apply basic CRM principles to build customer relationships
4. Apply basic GDPR principles to process customer data
5. Create a customer feedback survey
6. Reflect on how CRM practices contribute to business growth

Customer Relationship Management (CRM) is the ability to build and maintain good relationships with customers before, during, and after a sale. It involves adapting to customer needs and offering a consistent experience. Successful customer relationship management leads to repeat business, word-of-mouth referrals, and a stronger reputation.
This skill can be especially important for you as a migrant entrepreneur, when trying to gain trust and overcome communication barriers with new customers in a new market.
Example: Layla runs a small hair salon out of her home. While she is happy that her business is growing, Layla finds it challenging to keep track of her customers.
Layla decides to create a simple record of her clients' names, phone numbers and service preferences, with their consent. She uses a notebook that is stored safely when not in use.

The record enables Layla to remember her clients' needs and create a personal connection. She sends a polite-follow up message after appointments and offers small discounts to repeat customers. Over time Layla builds a loyal customer base, with customers recommending her business to others.
CRM does not require expensive software. Start small with personal actions to build customer loyalty and trust.
GDPR tips about keeping customer information:

items: Explain why you want to store your customers information. Explain what types of information you want to store, like preferences and phone numbers.
Ask for consent. Verbal consent can be sufficient.
Store the data in a safe way, and delete it if customers ask you to.

blocks.definition: Always greet and welcome clients. Make eye contact.
Be mindful of customers' suggestions and feedback, even unspoken ones. Try to understand what customers like and dislike.
Send reminders and updates. Check in after service.
Use a notebook, spreadsheet, or free CRM app to keep track of key customer information like names and numbers. Note preferences and feedback.
Be reliable in quality, attitude and pricing, so customers know what to expect.
When receiving complaints, respond in a calm and respectful manner. Offer solutions and resolve misunderstandings.

items: Practice small talk in the local language by conversing with people you meet.
Practice short customer conversations in the local language, including greeting, thanking and following up with customers.
Create simple templates for customer conversations in the local language, that you can follow.
Ask customers for feedback by sending them a friendly message or use a form. Thank customers for their input.
Keep track of customer information by using a notebook, spreadsheet or a CRM tool.
Observe how others practice customer relationship management. If needed, adjust your approach to adapt to local customs and expectations.
Ask for feedback with open questions, like: “How was everything today?”

“I don't know the language well enough.” o Prioritize learning some key phrases. Look for body language cues. Use websites or apps for translation. You do not have to be perfect; people will appreciate the effort you are making to speak a new language.
“I feel uncomfortable asking for feedback.” o Start by using friendly and neutral phrases like "Was everything okay for you today?" You can also invite feedback by using digital or printed forms.
“I can't remember my customers' names." o Use a notebook or other CRM tool to record names and preferences. Write things down immediately after a visit or call.
“Customers never respond to my follow-ups.” o Keep trying but stay polite. One message is usually enough.

blocks.definition: You made a mistake when completing an order. The customer has now returned to complain about it.
Team up in pairs and roleplay the scenario. One plays the dissatisfied customer, the other the salesperson.

blocks.text: Goals for the salesperson

items: Listen to the customer without interrupting
Thank the customer for the feedback
Apologize sincerely
Offer a solution to the problem

blocks.title: Try it
blocks.text: Switch roles and do the roleplay again, so both try to be the salesperson.
After the roleplay, discuss

items: What went well?
What was difficult?
Did you notice anything that was especially useful when dealing with the complaint? Any phrases or strategies?
I greet and thank customers
I speak politely and make eye contact
I keep track of my regular customers and their preferences
I follow up with at least some of my customers after providing a service or product
I listen calmly when I receive complaints and offer solutions to problems
I make customers feel respected and welcome
I am reliable and offer the same level of service every time

blocks.text: Customer relationship management is an important part of running a business. It can even be more powerful than advertising. The more trust you build with your customers, the more likely they are to come again and recommend you to others.

Customer relationship management is a skill that improves with practise. Focus on being kind, respectful and reliable, and pay attention to details. Welcome customers, invite feedback and follow-up after sales. You can use a CRM tool, but using a notebook or spreadsheet goes a long way. You will get better with every customer interaction!
After completing this module, participants are expected to
• Communicate more professionally with customers
• Handle customer complaints and conflicts more constructively
• Process and store customer data more responsibly
• Use feedback and follow-up strategies to strengthen customer relationships
